sources.title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing
Diagnosing sample ratio mismatch in online controlled experiments

concepts.definition: A randomized controlled experiment comparing a control and a changed version on a predefined metric.
A difference between the planned and the observed split of traffic, which signals a broken test.
Checking results repeatedly and stopping when they look significant, which inflates false positives.

questions.q: With a 3% baseline conversion rate, about how many visitors per group are needed to detect a 10% relative lift?
questions.a: About 52,000 per group, using n = 16 x p(1 - p) / delta squared with delta = 0.003.

questions.q: Why does randomization make the comparison fair?
questions.a: It spreads differences such as season, traffic source and user type evenly between groups on average, so the remaining difference can be attributed to the change.
